text: But the Israelites broke faith concerning the things devoted to destruction. Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was devoted, and the LORD's anger burned against the Israelites.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which lies near Beth Aven, east of Bethel, and told them, "Go up and scout out the land." So the men went up and scouted Ai.

When they returned to Joshua they said, "There is no need for the whole army to go up. Send about two or three thousand men to attack Ai. Do not wear out the whole army there, for the people of Ai are few."
So about three thousand men went up—and they fled before the men of Ai.
The men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them, chasing them from the gate as far as Shebarim and cutting them down on the slope. At this the hearts of the people melted and turned to water.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown on the ground before the ark of the LORD until evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they threw dust on their heads.

And Joshua said, "Alas, Lord GOD, why did you ever bring this people across the Jordan—only to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!
O Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned its back before its enemies?
The Canaanites and all who live in the land will hear of it. They will surround us and wipe our name from the earth. And then what will you do for your great name?"
The LORD said to Joshua, "Stand up! Why are you lying facedown?

Israel has sinned. They have violated my covenant, which I commanded them to keep. They have taken some of what was devoted to destruction; they have stolen, they have lied, they have put it among their own possessions.

That is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies. They turn their backs and run, because they themselves have now become devoted to destruction. I will not be with you any longer unless you destroy whatever among you is devoted to destruction.

versions.text: That is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies. They turn their backs and run, because they themselves have come under the ban. I will not be with you any longer unless you destroy whatever among you is devoted to destruction.
versions.explanation: The phrase "come under the ban" introduces a technical term ("the ban") that appears nowhere else in the chapter, where חֵרֶם is consistently rendered "devoted to destruction." Consistent wording helps the hearer connect Israel's fate to Achan's sin.

text: Get up! Consecrate the people. Say to them, 'Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, because this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: There is devoted property among you, Israel. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove it from your midst.'

In the morning you shall come forward tribe by tribe. The tribe the LORD singles out shall come forward clan by clan; the clan the LORD singles out shall come forward household by household; and the household the LORD singles out shall come forward man by man.
The one who is caught with the devoted things shall be burned with fire, he and all that belongs to him, because he has violated the covenant of the LORD and has done an outrageous thing in Israel."
Early the next morning Joshua had Israel come forward by tribes, and the tribe of Judah was singled out.
He brought forward the clans of Judah, and the clan of the Zerahites was singled out. He brought the clan of the Zerahites forward man by man, and Zabdi was singled out.
Joshua brought his household forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was singled out.
Then Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and make confession to him. Tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me."
Achan answered Joshua, "It is true. I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did:

Among the spoil I saw a beautiful robe from Babylonia, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels. I coveted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath."
Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. There it was, hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.
They took the things from the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and spread them out before the LORD.

Then Joshua, together with all Israel, took Achan son of Zerah, along with the silver, the robe, and the bar of gold, his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys and sheep, his tent and everything he had, and brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said, "Why have you brought this disaster on us? Today the LORD brings disaster on you." Then all Israel pelted him with stones, and they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.

versions.text: Joshua said, "Why have you brought this disaster on us? Today the LORD brings disaster on you." Then all Israel stoned him, and after they had stoned the rest, they burned them.
versions.explanation: The current rendering reverses the Hebrew sequence (stoning, then burning, then stoning) and adds "the rest," which is not in the text and reads as an interpretive expansion. A rendering that keeps the Hebrew order avoids adding content.

versions.text: Joshua said, "Why have you brought this disaster on us? Today the LORD brings disaster on you." Then all Israel stoned him to death, and they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew simply says all Israel pelted him with stone(s); "to death" is an added interpretive element, and it sits awkwardly before the burning and further stoning that follow. Rendering the first verb as "pelted him with stones" keeps the content exact and also varies the three verbs naturally for oral reading.

text: Over him they piled a great heap of stones, which remains to this day. Then the LORD turned from his fierce anger. That is why the place has been called the Valley of Achor ever since.
